description: End-to-end, code-first tutorials for building production-grade GenAI agents. From prototype to enterprise deployment.

summary.one_liner: A collection of code-first, notebook-based tutorials for building and deploying production-grade GenAI agents, from prototype to enterprise deployment.
summary.what_it_does: The repository is organized as roughly 28 tutorials, each in its own folder with runnable notebooks or code files, grouped by topic: tool integration, data processing, RAG and knowledge management, memory, deployment, multi-agent coordination, GPU deployment, security, agent frameworks, model customization, tracing and debugging, evaluation, and UI. Covered topics named in the README include stateful workflows with LangGraph, vector memory (Redis, Mem0, Cognee), MCP tool integration, A2A multi-agent communication, Docker containers, FastAPI endpoints, Ollama local models, AWS Bedrock AgentCore deployment, LlamaFirewall guardrails, LangSmith tracing, IntellAgent evaluation, and a Streamlit chatbot. Several tutorials are written by commercial sponsors and feature their platforms (for example Arcade, Bright Data, Tavily, Inngest, Contextual AI, Runpod). The README also promotes the author's companion books and a newsletter, which are not part of the code.
use_cases: Learning to build a stateful LangGraph agent workflow
Adding vector or graph memory to an agent
Containerizing and deploying an agent with Docker or FastAPI
Adding security guardrails against prompt injection
Running open-source LLMs locally with Ollama
how_to_run: cd tutorials/<tutorial-folder> (choose the tutorial you want)
pip install -r requirements.txt (inside the tutorial folder, if provided)
notable: Tutorials are runnable notebooks or code, each in its own folder, rather than prose-only guides
Covers the full agent stack from orchestration and memory to security, tracing, evaluation, and deployment
Includes a durable RAG ingestion tutorial that measures failure costs before fixing them with idempotent upserts
Some tutorials are contributed by sponsoring companies and center on their products
caveats: Licensed under a custom non-commercial license per the README, not a standard open-source license
Several tutorials depend on third-party commercial platforms or paid services (e.g. managed RAG, GPU cloud, AWS)
The README is mostly marketing and book promotion; the Quick Setup example uses a placeholder git clone command with no URL
